sources.title: Disclosure is not documentation: an open science framework for documenting generative AI use in scholarly research and publication workflows
sources.scope: Full main article text, references, declarations and Tables 1–7; all text of Additional file 1 (AI-use documentation, manuscript V4.1, updated 7 August 2026). Additional file 2 (57-page AI-generated exploratory mapping) downloaded but only introductory/search-method text read. External OSF package not inspected. Full-text reading is not a validation of the article or its mapping.
sources.note: Tables 6–7 already cover verification, accepted/modified/rejected outputs, influence on claims, prompt chains and review histories. The author’s own human-generated initial text describes that article’s practice; the framework also covers substantive AI drafting.

sources.title: An experimental evaluation of the assumption of independence in multiversion programming
sources.scope: Selected full-text inspection of the 47-page manuscript hosted by Rutgers: abstract, introduction excerpts, section 6 fault examples (printed pp. 16-17), and section 8 conclusions (printed pp. 19-21). The complete specification appendix was not read; no experimental replay.
sources.note: Separately developed versions failed dependently in this experiment. The authors explicitly reject specification deficiencies as the explanation for the observed common faults; examples concern numerical analysis and incomplete geometry case analysis. A flawed shared brief remains a separate possible scenario, not the mechanism established here.

inspection_history.note: 27 independently written versions from one specification, one million tests; coincident failures substantially exceeded what independence predicts. Cited in docs/warrant-and-independence.md for common-mode failure.

sources.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
sources.scope: Selected full-text HTML of arXiv:2506.07962v1 (9 June 2025): abstract, sections 1, 3-4, relevant section 5.2 results and section 6 limitations; not a full reading of appendices or a data/code replay.
sources.note: HELM's 0.60 is pairwise answer agreement conditional on both models erring, not the probability that an agreed answer is wrong. Section 4 recommends ground-truth calibration of model-judge pairs. Section 6 identifies limitations of the correlation metric and the restricted multiple-choice/offline task settings. These data do not calibrate this project's current long-form model reviews.

sources.title: GAIDeT (Generative AI Delegation Taxonomy): A taxonomy for humans to delegate tasks to generative artificial intelligence in scientific research and publishing
sources.version: Publisher PDF, 28 PDF pages including cover and article pp. 1–27; minor-correction notice present
sources.scope: Complete main article PDF text, Table 1, declarations and references read. Supplementary File 1 was not retrieved. Publisher HTML first returned HTTP 403; direct publisher PDF subsequently succeeded. Institutional repository explicitly had no full text; supplementary-page retrieval yielded no usable supplement.
sources.note: Source ID retains first-online year 2025; assigned issue is 2026. Section 4.3 limits delegable tasks on capability grounds. Section 5.1 proposes contribution fractions for discussion, not a settled measurement rule. Section 5.4 explicitly separates task classification from assessing scholarly quality.
